Drugs 1991; 42: 825–76. 2. Onrust SV, et al. Ofloxacin: a reappraisal of its use in the man- agement of genitourinary tract infections. Drugs 1998; 56: 895–928. 3. Simpson KL, Markham A. Drug Safety 2003; 26: 405–20. Administration in hepatic impairment. The clearance of ofloxacin is reduced in patients with severe hepatic impairment or cirrhosis and lower doses should be used; a maximum dose of 400 mg daily has been recommended. Administration in renal impairment. Lower doses of ofloxacin may be necessary in patients with renal impairment. After the usual initial dose (see above), subsequent doses are ad- justed according to creatinine clearance (CC): • CC 20 to 50 mL/minute: doses halved to 100 to 200 mg daily or the usual dose is given every 24 hours • CC less than 20 mL/minute: dose reduced to 100 mg every 24 hours • patients on haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis: 100 mg eve- ry 24 hours BCG toxicity. For mention of the possible use of ofloxacin to reduce the incidence of toxicity after BCG intravesicular instilla- tion, see p.2206. Preparations USP 31: Ofloxacin Ophthalmic Solution; Ofloxacin Tablets.
